subject: Nightly batch window: 504 spikes & throughput collapse — urgent customer escalation
messages:
From: ops@everwell.ai
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 22 Sep 2028 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Production: massive 504s + p99 latency spike during nightly batch window

Alex / Ben —

We're seeing a severe degradation in inference performance during our nightly batch window that started ~02:00 local (UTC-7) and persisted for ~90 minutes. Summary: p99 jumped to ~18s (normal ~450ms), error rate (5xx) spiked to 12%, and overall throughput dropped by ~60%. We attached a small diagnostic (everwell_hol_dump_20280922.json.gz) with request traces and KV cache metrics.

Key observations from our side:
- Elevated KV cache eviction rate and repeated prefix misses for a small set of heavy keys (hot-user segments).
- Many requests appear to be waiting behind a single hot key (head-of-line blocking) — stack traces show long waits in the runtime's KV lookup path.
- Batching appears to have amplified the issue: large batch sizes correlated with the 504 spike.

This is impacting production customers. Can you confirm immediate mitigation steps and ETA? We are open to temporary routing/fallbacks while you investigate.

Thanks,
Sam Patel
SRE Lead — Everwell AI

Attachments: everwell_hol_dump_20280922.json.gz (log excerpts)
From: alex_martinez@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 Sep 2028 09:35:10 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Production: massive 504s + p99 latency spike during nightly batch window

Forwarding Everwell's urgent alert — they attached traces showing KV eviction storms and clear HOL symptoms. Ben opened the case earlier today and has the account context.

Immediate asks:
1) Engineering runbook (Marissa) — can we push a short-lived mitigation to reduce batch size and disable aggressive prefetch for the Everwell tenant? Suggest: batch_size -> 1.5x smaller per lane, prefetch_window -> 0, hot-key guard TTL -> 30s.
2) Routing fallback — if mitigation doesn't stabilize within 15 minutes, fallback Everwell to a higher-capacity model variant (redwood-13b-large) and limit concurrency by tenant.
3) Exec notification — Jonas, this is likely to need credits/comp and a post-mortem; want to loop you in for the customer call.

I attached a quick timeline CSV from their dump and a proposed config diff (kv-config-diff.patch).

On Fri, Sep 22, 2028 at 09:12 AM ops@everwell.ai wrote:
> Alex / Ben —
> 
> We're seeing a severe degradation ... (see original).
> 
> Sam

Attachments: timelines.csv, kv-config-diff.patch
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 Sep 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: massive 504s + p99 latency spike during nightly batch window

Thanks Alex — I have ops on standby to execute mitigations. Plan of action:

1) Apply emergency tenant overrides for Everwell (now):
   - per-tenant max_batch_tokens = 512 -> 192
   - disable async prefetch for that tenant
   - increase kv_cache_slots for hot-lane to 4x and set hot-key isolation TTL = 30s

2) Short-term routing: if p99 > 5s after 10 minutes, shift traffic to redwood-13b-large on dedicated pool and cap concurrency to 20 RPS.

3) Engineering debug: marissa -> I will collect HOT key list and run a KV eviction trace. We will instrument additional metrics (kv_evict_per_min, kv_prefetch_firing) and surface to Console.

Ben — please confirm customer outreach and schedule a call for immediate sync (they asked for an ETA).
On Fri, Sep 22, 2028 at 09:35 AM alex_martinez@redwood.com wrote:
> Forwarding Everwell's urgent alert — they attached traces ...
> 
> Alex

Attachments: kv-config-diff.patch
From: ops@everwell.ai
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 23 Sep 2028 15:10:05 +0100
Subject: Re: Production: massive 504s + p99 latency spike during nightly batch window

Alex / Marissa / Team —

Thanks for the fast response — after you applied the per-tenant overrides we saw a solid improvement in latency (p99 down to ~1.2s) and throughput recovered to ~90% of normal during a short A/B. However, we still observed intermittent 504s tied to a different hot key sequence (appears to be model-internal KV churn during long-context requests).

We need two things from Redwood:
- A short-term goodwill credit for the customer for the outage window (they lost batch processing for ~1.5 hours overnight).
- A scheduled post-mortem with engineering to review root cause and a timeline for a permanent fix (hot-key isolation at runtime or a stronger hot-lane throttle).
I attached a small PDF with customer request for credits and the sections of their logs that still show 504s.
Sam

Attachments: customer_request_credit.pdf

1) Provide 1 month of credits to Everwell for the affected billing window. Ben, coordinate PR/finance messaging and get the approval queued.
2) Schedule a customer-facing post-mortem this week (Marissa/Engineering + Everwell SRE). Outline: timeline, mitigation taken, root cause hypotheses, and three-month remediation plan.
